newsitem.title: USA: Kansas wheat seeding virtually complete.
newsitem.headline: Kansas wheat seeding virtually complete.

text.p: Seeding of the Kansas wheat crop was virtually complete during the week ended Sunday, the weekly state crop report said.

Wet conditions continued to prevent completion of seeding in east central and south eastern districts. Wheat diseases such as stem rust, wheat streak mosaic and septoria have been found over much of the state.
Because of excellent fall crop production, elevators were full in some locations, the report said.
Kansas wheat was rated 89 percent good to excellent, versus 91 percent at that level last week.
Wheat seeding was 99 percent complete, versus 98 last week, 100 a year ago and 99 on average. Wheat was 97 percent emerged, versus 95 last week, 92 last year and 90 on average.

Corn was 97 percent harvested versus 93 last week, 97 last year and the average of 94 percent. Sorghum was 86 percent harvested, versus 77 last week, 97 last year and the average of 85 percent. Soybeans were 88 percent harvested, versus 82 last week, 99 last year and 94 on average.
Pasture condition was rated 69 percent good to excellent, versus 74 at that level last week.
